name: level1-win-conservative
description: Level 1 (Dusty Hollow): 4 small blasts and 2 contract attempts -- named for a conservative win, but no hauling infrastructure means no delivery ever succeeds; see Findings #52-#53 for why the real trajectory (a net cash loss, well short of the $80k target) was originally asserted instead of the named outcome. #553: drilling now requires a licensed driller and a drill_rig, so exactly one vehicle is now bought where the file previously bought none -- the file's own point (no hauling infrastructure, so no delivery ever succeeds) is unchanged, but the real trajectory is far worse: the single rig ends up parked on the pattern it just drilled when the first blast fires (same mechanic tutorial-playthrough documents) and is destroyed, and because this file never buys a replacement, the remaining 3 drill_plan calls only ever order ghost holes nothing can claim. Combined with the driller's own payroll/fuel drain and the same unlucky contract-expiry fines Findings #52-#53 already documented, the level ends deeply in the red -- see the final campaign status step.

Vehicle #1, and the last one: this file's premise (no hauling infrastructure, so no delivery ever succeeds) depends on never buying a debris_hauler, rock_digger or rock_fragmenter either, and per its own instructions this file does not buy a replacement rig even after this one is destroyed below.

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:2 cols:2 spacing:3 depth:6 diameter:0.089 start:72,26
steps.description: #553: pattern relocated from (10,10)-(14,14) to (72,26)-(76,30) -- a uniform +62x/+16z shift applied to all four of this file's patterns (see the other three drill_plan steps below). Pre-#553 the absolute position never mattered, since confirming a plan wrote every hole into state in the same frame; now a driller has to physically drive there, and the driller/drill_rig both spawn at the nearest walkable cell to this site's grid centre, sandbox-measured at (82,34) (NavGrid.findNearestReachableCell anchored at the map corner -- the pit's own centre is unwalkable, so this is the real reachable point, not (48,48)). The original corner-clustered coordinates (x:8-28, z:8-28) are ~70 tiles from there; a direct trace with the un-shifted coordinates has the lone driller not even finishing this smallest 4-hole pattern until tick ~240, by which point the level has already gone bankrupt (cash crossed below $5,000 around tick 130 and the 100-tick grace period, BANKRUPTCY_GRACE_TICKS in balance.ts, elapses at tick 240) without a single blast fired. Shifting every pattern to sit around the real spawn point is what a player would actually do once drilling costs real travel time, and keeps this file's four blasts happening at all -- see the tick step immediately below for the measured landing time at the new site. Holes are ghosts until the driller drives there, hence orderedHoleCount rather than holeCount here (#553).

#553: sandbox-measured -- the single driller/drill_rig lands all 4 holes of this pattern by tick 40 (H4 at 13, H1 at 20, H2 at 25, H3 at 32); tick 50 is the pad. Cash keeps draining under the pad ($4/tick fuel+maintenance on the rig, $60/tick averaged driller payroll) even after the holes land, which is why cash is asserted as decreased rather than pinned to the exact pad-dependent figure.

role: player (issue #515): the Charge step's amount/stemming steppers and product-card explosive selector are real controls — this reaches the declared explosive/amount/stemming via clicks instead of Charge All using whatever the panel's fields already showed. Sandbox-measured: charging pop_rock at this amount costs nothing here (cash unchanged before/after in both this file's pre-#553 version and a direct #553 trace) -- unlike tutorial-playthrough's boomite charge, whatever pricing this leaves at $0 for this explosive/amount combination, not an authoring oversight.

Sequence's delay-step stepper carries data-field="delay-step" (Sequence.ts) for unambiguous click targeting. 1 increment click: 25ms default -> 30 (DELAY_STEP_INCREMENT=5ms, Sequence.ts). dstepMs is a plain instance field with no reset path (Finding #75/level1-lose-revolt.json) -- this file's later delay_step:25 occurrence below relies on it moving back down.

expect.note: #553: the sole driller and the sole drill_rig both end this blast right where the driller just finished drilling (a real trace: emp#1 never leaves (82,34), veh#1 ends at (72,29), one of this pattern's own 4 holes), the same unavoidable mechanic tutorial-playthrough's Finding documents (nothing in the UI relocates a vehicle before firing). deathCount stays 0 -- re-verified via a direct trace of state.damage: the destroyed rig is a vehicle_destroyed accident, not an injury/death (the driller's own tracked position is not inside the cleared voxels). vehicleCount drops 1->0 here (confirmed via `vehicle list`: "No vehicles.") -- not asserted (this file has no vehicleCount checks anywhere), but it is what makes every remaining drill_plan below order holes nothing can ever claim, since this file's own point requires never buying a second rig.

#553: safety is still 50 here -- the vehicle_destroyed accident from the blast above only starts costing safety on the ticks that follow (ScoreManager.ts: recentAccidents * 5 per tick against every accident inside the last 10 ticks), checked on the next tick step. wellBeing has already climbed from the fresh-hire baseline of 50 purely from the driller's own morale ticking up while working; ecology/nuisance are untouched -- this file's one real blast (4 holes, pop_rock) never triggers a vibration hit in a direct trace, unlike the original file's larger boomite blasts.

#553: confirmed via direct trace -- safety collapses from 50 toward 0 over these 20 ticks (recentAccidents * 5 per tick, ScoreManager.ts, against the single vehicle_destroyed accident from the blast above, which stays "recent" for its own 10-tick window) -- the same mechanism tutorial-playthrough's two-death blast documents, just from property damage instead of a death. cash keeps draining from ordinary driller payroll/fuel even with nothing left to do.

#553: contract id renumbered 1 -> 3 -- the extra travel/landing ticks this file now spends (the driller/rig now take real time to reach and sink each pattern) push this checkpoint's tickCount from the original file's 40 to 90, and the pool refreshes on its own clock (CONTRACT_REFRESH_INTERVAL=20, CONTRACTS_PER_REFRESH=3) independent of anything this file does, so ids 1 and 2 are long gone from it by now. #3 (sparkium, 420kg @ $237.60/kg, 42-tick deadline, $29,937 penalty) is genuinely first in the live pool at this tick -- probed via `contract list`. Coincidentally the same commodity/penalty the original file's Finding #53 called out as its 'accept whatever renders first' risk, just landing at this file's first contract stage instead of its second. #513/#581: the accept click is scoped to `[data-contract-id="3"]`, the contract this step's `command` names -- unscoped, `.bs-contract-accept` always resolves to whichever offered card is first in the DOM, so scoping keeps both channels testing the same acceptance.

BLOCKED, and deliberately not converted to a click: the ACTIVE card's DELIVER button is genuinely disabled at this point. ContractsPanel disables the amount box, MAX and DELIVER together whenever maxDeliverable = min(contract remaining, stored material) is 0, and a direct trace of this file shows 0.0 kg of sparkium in storage against this contract -- the single driller this file hires never touches hauling, and no debris_hauler is ever bought. The console command is no better: it returns success:false ("Not enough sparkium in storage: 0.0 kg available, 300.0 kg requested") and command mode only fails a step on a thrown exception, so this is a silent no-op in BOTH modes today. `expect.blocked` is what now pins it down -- the button must be in the DOM and refused, with `expect.usable` on the panel's own storage link proving the panel is really open, so "blocked" cannot pass just because nothing is on screen.

expect.note: stays active/undelivered -- economy-full-loop.json is the file that actually hauls stock and completes a delivery.

#553, superseding Findings #52-#53: this file used to never hire anyone or buy a vehicle at all, and ended at a bruised but positive $11,867 -- almost entirely from two expired-contract fines and one weather event, never from any operating cost, since nothing in the file ever cost anything to run. Drilling now requires exactly one driller and one drill_rig (the file's own point -- no OTHER hauling infrastructure, so no delivery ever succeeds -- is otherwise unchanged), and that single rig ends up parked on the pattern it just drilled when the first blast fires, destroying it (same mechanic tutorial-playthrough's Finding documents) with no replacement bought after. The other three drill/charge/sequence/blast cycles this file's own description promises still run, but operate on zero real holes throughout: BAD/$0 blast reports, DETONATE disabled at the panel (`expect.blocked`, not a click), nothing to charge or sequence. Real costs this file never used to pay -- $1,000 to hire, $35,000 for the rig, ~$60/tick combined payroll and fuel for 215 ticks -- combine with the SAME class of contract-expiry fine Finding #53 flagged (this run: $29,937 sparkium, $31,505 craktonite, $136 rubble) and one union_lunch_thief event (-$1,200) to leave cash at -$61,808: a real net loss of $111,808 against the level's $80,000 target, not just a shortfall. deathCount stays 0 (re-verified via direct trace of state.damage after every blast -- the driller is never standing in the cleared voxels, only the vehicle is) -- the file's one employee survives the whole run. bankrupt/levelEnded both stay false: cash first crossed below BANKRUPTCY_THRESHOLD ($5,000) around tick 130 and never recovered, but BANKRUPTCY_GRACE_TICKS (100 consecutive ticks below threshold) had not yet elapsed by the final tick (215) -- confirmed via direct trace, ticksBelowThreshold sits around 85. No ecological/revolt shutdown either -- the one real blast never moved ecology/nuisance off the fresh-game baseline of 50.
